segment: People in NSW choosing a new-build home design (and the builder staff whose designs appear on SHOWHAUS unclaimed)
grounding: Phrasing lifted from Australian builder and industry pages on display homes and virtual tours (G.J. Gardner, Montgomery Homes, The Good Builder, homeshelf, Lifesize Plans reviews). Reddit threads could not be reached from this session, so no Reddit quotes are in this panel.

attrs: first-home buyer with partner, land settled 2 months ago
budget tight, every upgrade is weighed
tech comfort high, lives on her phone
has visited 2 display villages on weekends
patience medium
pays for apps occasionally (under $10)
says a floor plan 'fails to give the feel of a home'
personas.last_time: Took photos of every room in a display home and labelled them by builder, then still could not remember which was which.

attrs: knock-down rebuild, second home
budget comfortable
tech comfort high
impatient, decides fast
wants to save thousands by changing the design before the build, not at frame stage
happy to pay for something that prevents one variation fee
compares 4 builders
personas.last_time: Paid a draftsperson for a 3D model of the last house and thought it was value for money.

attrs: building on a block he already owns
distrusts renders: 'the display home is the upgraded version, not what you get'
tech comfort medium
will not pay for anything a builder should provide free
trusts walking a real display home and taking a tape measure
patience low
has been burned by a variation bill
personas.last_time: Drove 50 minutes to a display village to measure the kitchen himself.

attrs: downsizing to a single-storey design
tech comfort low: uses Facebook and email, pinch-zoom confuses her
budget fine
wants to know if her furniture fits and where the sun comes in
patience high but gives up quietly if lost
asks her daughter before paying online
finds floor plans hard to read
personas.last_time: Asked the sales consultant to walk her through the printed plan twice.

attrs: house-and-land package buyer with two kids
tech comfort very high
price sensitive but pays for tools that save weekends
reads every disclaimer
has used builder virtual tours (Matterport style) of real display homes
notices fake-looking renders immediately
patience medium
personas.last_time: Used a builder's virtual tour to rule out two designs without leaving the house.

attrs: already chose a builder and is happy with their own virtual tours
sees no reason for a third-party site
tech comfort high
will not enter card details on a site she has not heard of
wary of AI images: 'is this the actual house or made up?'
patience low
values accuracy over prettiness
personas.last_time: Used her builder's own 3D tour and the display home; felt that was enough.

attrs: regional build, nearest display village is 4 hours away
tech comfort low, big-font phone, taps the wrong thing often
budget modest
cannot visit display homes easily, so anything he can see from home matters
does not know what 'credits' means
patience medium
would rather ring someone
personas.last_time: Chose between two plans from the brochure because he could not get to the display home.

personas.who: Jess, 29, marketing coordinator at a mid-size NSW project builder
attrs: found her company's design on the site by accident
owns the builder's website and socials
tech comfort high
small monthly marketing budget she can spend without sign-off
measured on enquiry numbers
protective of brand: wrong finishes on a design is a problem
knows display homes cost a fortune and cannot show every design
personas.last_time: Paid a rendering studio for stills of three designs that have no display home.

personas.who: Greg, 55, sales manager at a volume builder
attrs: irritated that a third party is showing his design without asking
thinks about calling legal
tech comfort medium
believes buyers need to walk a real display home to trust workmanship
has an existing virtual-tour supplier
no patience for start-ups
would only act if it brought enquiries
personas.last_time: Signed a yearly contract with a virtual tour company for the flagship displays.

personas.who: Amira, 38, owner of a small custom home builder, Western Sydney
attrs: no display home, cannot afford one
sells from plans and past jobs
tech comfort medium
spends on anything that gets a client to sign sooner
does her own marketing at night
clients struggle to visualise from paper plans
careful with money but decisive
personas.last_time: Borrowed a friend's SketchUp model to show a client the living area.

personas.who: Liam, 27, renter in Marrickville, not buying
attrs: came from the SHOWHAUS rent map
browses homes for fun
tech comfort high
would not pay for anything about a home he is not buying
short attention, leaves in under a minute if bored
likes games, WASD is natural
shares funny or impressive links with friends
personas.last_time: Scrolled real-estate listings on the train with no intention to buy.

attrs: works with renovation clients, not project builders
makes her own renders, knows what good looks like
tech comfort high
pays for tools that win a client meeting
critical eye for wrong proportions and fake light
curious whether she could upload a client's plan
bills by the hour, values speed
personas.last_time: Spent a day building a 3D model to settle a client's doubt about a kitchen layout.
